newsitem.title: INDIA: India revises royalty rates for gold, silver.
newsitem.headline: India revises royalty rates for gold, silver.

text.p: The Indian Mines Ministry on Thursday said the new royalty rate payable to states for primary gold would be 1.5 percent of the metal sale price, following a revision of royalty rates for major minerals.
A ministry statement said the rate on gold by-products would be 2.5 percent of the metal sale price while it would be five percent of the sale price for silver.
The Mines Ministry on Wednesday revised the royalty rates payable to states for major minerals by eight to 14 percent, the ministry said in a statement.

"The increase in royalty rates is generally in the range of eight percent to 14 percent and the royalty accruals to the state governments from major minerals per year would go up by more than one billion rupees ($28 million)," the ministry said.
The rates were last revised in February 1992.
The ministry said 17 rates were fixed on an ad valorem basis to eliminate the need for multiple rates and shore up state government revenues.
The royalty rate for copper concentrate would be 0.7 percent of the London Metal Exchange metal price on an ad valorem basis chargeable per tonne of concentrate produced.
The rate for nickel ore will be 2.25 rupees per unit percent of contained nickel metal per tonne of ore and on a pro-rata basis.
The new rates for manganese ore range from two rupees to 112 rupees per tonne and from six rupees to 21.50 rupees per tonne for iron ore.
Under the Indian constitution, royalty is levied by the federal government and revenue is handed over to the states where the minerals are extracted.
